title: A Machine-to-Machine Knowledge-Guided LLM Agent for Generalizable Radiotherapy Treatment Planning
summary: In this work, we propose a prototype machine-to-machine (M2M) knowledge-guided Large Language Model (LLM) framework for automated radiotherapy treatment planning. In the proposed paradigm, Treatment Planning Parameter (TPP) distribution knowledge discovered by a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agent is transferred to an LLM agent through in-context learning, enabling autonomous iterative planning without human intervention. While standard LLM-based planning often lacks physical intuition and struggles with convergence, the integration of DRL-derived guidance constrains the agent to a physically valid parameter space. Experimental evaluations are performed across three diverse planning scenarios: basic prostate cases, complex prostate configurations with increased organ-at-risk (OAR) constraints, and liver cases. The evaluation results demonstrate that the guided LLM agent consistently achieves optimal planning scores while significantly reducing the number of iterations compared to unguided planning. Analysis of the final TPP configurations reveals that the agent successfully learns a hierarchical priority of objectives, effectively restoring a logical "cause-and-effect" relationship between parameter tuning and dosimetric outcomes. Crucially, this prototype framework exhibits robust generalizability, maintaining high planning quality regardless of specific patient anatomy, treatment site, or initial plan quality. By bridging the specialized optimization of DRL with the adaptive reasoning of LLMs, this M2M framework establishes a scalable foundation towards generalizable autonomous treatment planning, ultimately benefiting clinical practice in realistic environments.
tldr: A framework combining Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and Large Language Models (LLM) for automated radiotherapy treatment planning, achieving generalizability and efficiency by transferring DRL-derived knowledge to guide the LLM agent.
tldr_zh: 结合深度强化学习（DRL）和大型语言模型（LLM）的框架，通过将DRL导出的知识传递给LLM代理，实现自动化放射治疗计划，具有通用性和高效性。
summary_zh: 在本研究中，我们提出了一种面向自动化放射治疗计划的原型机器间（M2M）知识引导大语言模型（LLM）框架。在该范式中，通过深度强化学习（DRL）智能体发现的治疗计划参数（TPP）分布知识，借助上下文学习迁移至LLM智能体，从而实现在无人工干预下的自主迭代计划制定。尽管基于LLM的标准规划往往缺乏物理直觉且收敛困难，但整合DRL衍生的引导信息可将智能体约束在物理有效的参数空间内。实验评估涵盖了三种不同规划场景：基础前列腺病例、伴随器官危及（OAR）约束增加的复杂前列腺配置，以及肝脏病例。评估结果表明，与无引导规划相比，引导式LLM智能体始终能达到最优规划评分，同时显著减少迭代次数。对最终TPP配置的分析显示，该智能体成功学习了目标的层级优先级，有效恢复了参数调优与剂量学结果之间的逻辑"因果关系"。关键的是，该原型框架展现出强大的泛化能力，无论患者解剖结构、治疗部位或初始计划质量如何，均能保持高规划质量。通过弥合DRL的专门优化与LLM的适应性推理之间的鸿沟，该M2M框架为迈向可泛化的自主治疗计划奠定了可扩展基础，最终将惠及现实环境中的临床实践。

title: CAREAgent: Clinical Agent with Structured Reasoning and Tool-Integrated for Order Generation
summary: Clinical order generation serves as a critical bridge between clinical decision-making and real-world practice, translating medical decisions into concrete and executable orders. Existing agents mainly focus on coarse-grained decisions and overlook the fine-grained, executable information required for clinical orders. To address this gap, we propose CAREAgent, an agent for clinical order generation. To support its training, we introduce a two-stage agentic reasoning data construction method. First, we design an agent framework that constructs verifiable reasoning trajectories aligned with realistic clinical tool usage. Second, we filter reasoning trajectories by format compliance, order validity, and clinical plausibility. Building on the constructed data, the model is first trained via supervised fine-tuning to acquire fundamental reasoning formats and medical knowledge, and is subsequently optimized through reinforcement learning with multi-dimensional reward functions to enhance complex clinical reasoning capabilities. Experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of CAREAgent. On ClinicalBench (unseen during training), CAREAgent improves the F1 score by 5.05%, 2.09%, and 0.86% over the single-agent, multi-agent, and agentic reasoning methods, respectively.
tldr: CAREAgent is a clinical agent for order generation that uses a two-stage data construction method (verifiable reasoning trajectories with tool use, then filtering) and trains via supervised fine-tuning plus reinforcement learning, achieving improved F1 scores on ClinicalBench.
tldr_zh: CAREAgent是一个用于医嘱生成的临床代理，采用两阶段数据构建方法（结合工具使用的可验证推理轨迹，然后过滤），并通过监督微调加强化学习训练，在ClinicalBench上取得了改进的F1分数。
summary_zh: 摘要：临床医嘱生成是连接临床决策与实际操作的关键桥梁，将医疗决策转化为具体且可执行的医嘱。现有智能体主要关注粗粒度决策，忽视了临床医嘱所需的细粒度、可执行信息。为弥补这一不足，我们提出了CAREAgent，一种用于临床医嘱生成的智能体。为支持其训练，我们引入了一种两阶段智能体推理数据构建方法。首先，我们设计了一个智能体框架，构建与真实临床工具使用场景一致的可验证推理轨迹。其次，我们根据格式合规性、医嘱有效性和临床合理性对推理轨迹进行筛选。基于构建的数据，模型先通过监督微调获得基本推理格式和医学知识，随后通过多维奖励函数的强化学习进一步优化，以增强复杂临床推理能力。在多个基准测试上的实验证明了CAREAgent的有效性。在ClinicalBench（训练中未见数据）上，CAREAgent相较于单智能体、多智能体和智能体推理方法，F1分数分别提升了5.05%、2.09%和0.86%。

title: Interaction-Limited Safe Continuous-Time RL for Dynamical Medical Treatment
summary: Dynamic medical treatment requires deciding treatment intensity and intervention timing, while patient states evolve continuously and adverse events may occur between clinical interactions. Most existing treatment learning methods assume fixed schedules or enforce safety only at discrete decision points. We propose Interaction-Limited Safe Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning, a framework that jointly optimizes treatment administration and clinical interaction timing under trajectory-level safety constraints. Our key idea is to reformulate the continuous time treatment problem as an option-based semi-Markov decision process, where each option specifies a continuous-time treatment policy and its duration. We develop a safety-tightening mechanism showing that suitably constructed constraints at interaction times guarantee safety over the full continuous-time trajectory with high probability. We further establish finite-sample guarantees for policy learning from logged treatment trajectories and introduce a practical data-driven conservative surrogate. Experiments show that the proposed adaptive interaction-timing mechanism improves both safety and treatment effectiveness over equidistant interaction schemes across different safe policy optimization methods.
tldr: This paper proposes a continuous-time reinforcement learning framework for dynamic medical treatment that jointly optimizes treatment intensity and clinical visit timing under trajectory-level safety constraints, using an option-based semi-MDP and a safety-tightening mechanism with theoretical guarantees.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于动态医疗治疗的连续时间强化学习框架，联合优化治疗强度与临床就诊时机，并在轨迹层面满足安全约束，采用基于选项的半马尔可夫决策过程和安全收紧机制，并提供了理论保证。
summary_zh:
摘要：  
动态医疗决策需要同时确定治疗强度与干预时机，而患者状态持续演变，且不良事件可能在临床交互间隔期间发生。现有大多数治疗学习方法假设固定调度机制，或仅在离散决策点强制实施安全性约束。本文提出交互受限的安全连续时间强化学习框架，该框架在轨迹级安全约束下联合优化治疗实施与临床交互时机。核心思路是将连续时间治疗问题重新表述为基于选项的半马尔可夫决策过程，其中每个选项定义了连续时间治疗策略及其持续时间。我们开发了一种安全收紧机制，证明了在交互时刻合理构造的约束能够以高概率保证整个连续时间轨迹的安全性。进一步，我们建立了从历史治疗轨迹进行策略学习的有穷样本保证，并引入了一种实用的数据驱动保守替代方法。实验表明，在不同安全策略优化方法中，所提出的自适应交互时机机制相较于等间隔交互方案，在安全性和治疗效果上均有提升。

title: MedGym:A Unified Continuous-Time Benchmark for Dynamic Medical Treatment Reinforcement Learning
summary: Medical treatment recommendation poses several challenges to reinforcement learning (RL): patient physiology evolves in continuous time, measurements and interventions are performed at irregular intervals, and treatment effects vary substantially across individuals. Existing RL formulations and simulated environments, however, are based on discrete-time MDP or POMDP abstractions with fixed or pre-specified decision intervals. Thus, it remains difficult to evaluate whether RL methods can handle time-interval-dependent disease progression, personalized treatment response, and safety between consecutive measurement points. To address this gap, we introduce MedGym, a benchmark environment for dynamic treatment recommendation. MedGym models longitudinal patient evolution in a continuous-time framework and constructs a configurable medical RL benchmark from clinical data by using Physics-Informed Neural Networks. The resulting benchmark supports both offline and online RL, and enables direct comparison between discrete-time and continuous-time methods under irregular treatment timing and patient-specific dynamics. Besides, MedGym supports evaluation from clinically important perspectives, including personalization, trajectory-level safety, and the performance gap between model-based offline learning and online deployment. By providing a standardized and configurable benchmark for continuous-time dynamic treatment, MedGym aims to facilitate more realistic and informative evaluation of medical RL methods.
tldr: MedGym introduces a continuous-time benchmark for dynamic medical treatment RL, using Physics-Informed Neural Networks to model patient physiology from clinical data, supporting both offline and online RL with evaluations on personalization and safety.
tldr_zh: MedGym 提出了一个连续时间的医学治疗强化学习基准，利用物理信息神经网络从临床数据建模患者生理，支持离线与在线 RL，并评估个性化和安全性。
summary_zh: 医疗治疗推荐对强化学习（RL）提出了若干挑战：患者生理状态随时间连续变化，测量和干预以不规则的时间间隔进行，且治疗效果在个体间存在显著差异。然而，现有的RL框架和仿真环境均基于具有固定或预设决策间隔的离散时间MDP或POMDP抽象模型。因此，目前仍难以评估RL方法能否处理依赖时间间隔的疾病进展、个性化治疗反应以及连续测量点之间的安全性问题。为解决这一不足，我们提出了MedGym——一个用于动态治疗推荐的基准环境。MedGym在连续时间框架下对患者纵向演变进行建模，并利用物理信息神经网络从临床数据中构建了一个可配置的医疗RL基准。该基准同时支持离线RL和在线RL，并能够在不规则治疗时机和患者特异性动力学条件下，直接比较离散时间方法与连续时间方法。此外，MedGym还支持从临床重要角度进行评估，包括个性化、轨迹级安全性以及基于模型的离线学习与在线部署之间的性能差距。通过为连续时间动态治疗提供标准化且可配置的基准，MedGym旨在促进对医疗RL方法进行更真实、更具信息量的评估。

title: Med-HEAL: Analyzing and Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical LLMs with Hallucination-Aware In-Context Learning
summary:
Hallucinations in medical large language models (LLMs) pose serious risks for clinical decision support, particularly when models must reason over complex electronic health records (EHRs). However, existing benchmarks often lack a realistic clinical context and provide limited insight into how hallucinations can be mitigated in practice. We introduce Med-HEAL, a framework for systematically identifying, analyzing, and mitigating hallucinations in medical LLMs using clinically grounded data. Building on the EHRNoteQA benchmark derived from MIMIC-IV discharge summaries, we construct a hallucination dataset by evaluating BioMistral-7B on open-ended clinical question answering tasks. Model outputs are labeled through a dual evaluation pipeline that combines LLM-as-a-Judge assessment (GPT-4o) with human auditing by medical student reviewers, producing correctness judgments and annotations of reasoning errors via a custom web-based evaluation system.
  We then leverage this dataset to investigate mitigation strategies: a self-critique pipeline, in which the test model reviews its own answers to detect potential errors and regenerates responses for flagged cases, and retrieval-augmented in-context learning (RA-ICL), which exposes the model to hallucinated and corrected examples. Experiments across five open-source LLMs-BioMistral, Llama-3.1, DeepSeek, Qwen2.5, and Qwen3, show that the self-critique strategy improves accuracy for three of five models (p < 0.05) without requiring parameter updates.
  Med-HEAL provides both a reusable hallucination dataset and a practical framework for studying and mitigating hallucinations in medical LLMs, supporting safer deployment of AI systems in clinical environments. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/yimingliao-blad/med-heal.git.
tldr: Med-HEAL introduces a systematic framework to detect, analyze, and mitigate hallucinations in medical LLMs by creating a clinically grounded hallucination dataset from EHRNoteQA and evaluating self-critique and retrieval-augmented in-context learning strategies across five open-source models, showing significant accuracy improvements for three of them.
tldr_zh: Med-HEAL提出了一个系统性框架，通过从EHRNoteQA构建临床驱动的幻觉数据集，并在五个开源模型上评估自我批评和检索增强上下文学习策略，来检测、分析和减轻医学大语言模型中的幻觉，结果显示其中三个模型的准确率显著提升。
summary_zh: 摘要：医疗大语言模型（LLMs）中的幻觉问题对临床决策支持构成了严重风险，尤其是当模型需要基于复杂的电子健康记录（EHRs）进行推理时。然而，现有基准测试通常缺乏真实的临床背景，且对如何在实践中缓解幻觉所提供的见解有限。我们提出了Med-HEAL，一个利用临床基础数据系统性识别、分析和缓解医疗LLMs中幻觉的框架。基于源自MIMIC-IV出院小结的EHRNoteQA基准，我们通过让BioMistral-7B执行开放式临床问答任务，构建了一个幻觉数据集。模型输出通过一个双评估流程进行标注，该流程结合了LLM作为评判者（GPT-4o）的评估与医学生评审员的人工审核，借助自定义的基于Web的评估系统生成正确性判断和推理错误注释。随后，我们利用该数据集研究缓解策略：自我批判流程——测试模型自行审查其答案以检测潜在错误，并对标记案例重新生成响应；以及检索增强的上下文学习（RA-ICL）——让模型接触幻觉示例和修正后的示例。在五个开源LLM（BioMistral、Llama-3.1、DeepSeek、Qwen2.5和Qwen3）上的实验表明，自我批判策略在无需更新参数的情况下，使五个模型中的三个准确性得到提升（p < 0.05）。Med-HEAL既提供了一个可复用的幻觉数据集，也为研究和缓解医疗LLMs中的幻觉提供了实用框架，支持AI系统在临床环境中更安全地部署。我们的代码和数据于https://github.com/yimingliao-blad/med-heal.git公开提供。
